idea: Myers follows the furthest reachable position on each edit diagonal, extending equal-line runs for free. Backtracking produces a shortest insert/delete script.
steps: Tokenize documents as lines while preserving newline characters.
Expand edit-distance frontiers until the revised document is reached.
Backtrack, apply the patch and apply its inverse to verify both directions.
example:
Changing a
b to a
c requires one deletion and one insertion; replacement is not a primitive operation.
concepts: k=x−y identifies the difference between consumed source and target lines.
A maximal run of matching lines costs no edits.
A patch must consume the exact source lines it claims to delete or preserve.
question: Is a replacement one edit here?
answer: No. This model counts only insertions and deletions, so replacement costs two edits.
challenge: Try repeated lines and inspect one valid shortest script; ties can have different scripts.
cost: O((N+M)D) frontier work; saved backtracking frontiers use O(D²) memory; input is capped at 120 lines.
